questions.q: According to the research cited in this lesson, what effect does duplicate training data have on a model, beyond wasted compute?
options: It has no measurable effect beyond extra compute cost
It measurably increases the model's tendency to memorize duplicated content verbatim and can degrade overall quality
It always improves model quality by reinforcing important facts
It only affects the tokenizer, not the trained model
questions.explain: Lee et al.'s widely-cited study found duplicate content increases verbatim memorization and can degrade model quality relative to a deduplicated corpus of the same token count.

questions.q: What does exact deduplication via hashing catch, and what does it miss?
options: It catches everything, including near-duplicates with reworded sentences
It catches byte-for-byte (or lightly normalized) identical documents, but misses near-duplicates like reformatted or partially-edited copies
It catches only images, not text
It catches nothing useful and is never used in practice
questions.explain: Hashing normalized document text catches exact or near-exact duplicates cheaply, but two documents that differ even slightly (e.g., one changed sentence) will hash differently and won't be flagged.

questions.q: Why is comparing every document to every other document directly for similarity infeasible at web scale?
options: It would require quantum computers that don't exist yet
It is an O(n^2) problem that becomes computationally impossible at hundreds of millions or billions of documents
Text documents cannot be compared for similarity at all
It is actually feasible and commonly done this way in practice
questions.explain: Full pairwise comparison scales quadratically with the number of documents, making it computationally impossible at the scale of web-crawl corpora -- hence the need for MinHash and LSH.

questions.q: What does MinHash approximate when comparing two documents?
options: The exact byte-level difference between two files
Their Jaccard similarity (overlap of shingles/n-grams), using a compact fingerprint instead of the full text
The number of tokens in each document
The language each document is written in
questions.explain: MinHash computes a compact fingerprint from a set of hash-based minimum values such that the similarity between two documents' signatures approximates their true Jaccard similarity.

questions.q: What problem does Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) solve in the deduplication pipeline?
options: It encrypts documents so they cannot be read by unauthorized users
It buckets documents so only likely-similar pairs are ever compared directly, avoiding full pairwise comparison
It replaces the need for a tokenizer entirely
It automatically translates documents into English
questions.explain: LSH groups documents into buckets such that similar documents are likely to land in the same bucket, so only candidates within a bucket need direct comparison -- avoiding the O(n^2) cost of comparing everything.
